product.title: show me before I pay for a renovation
product.plus: People get these apps for one job: to see the room different before they spend money on a renovation or furniture. In RoomGPT one person writes that they were about to hire a designer for a new apartment, tried the app and bought things themselves, "saved hundreds of dollars." In AI Home Design DecAI they value exactly the ability to "see it before investing thousands and then realizing you hate it." In Remodel AI they praise being able to show a spouse who needs to "see it to commit."
product.minus: The moment the picture does not look like the real room, all the value collapses, because you can no longer make a decision from it. In Deko a person was flipping a house and without the paid version got "disappointing" pictures. In Interior with AI they write that all the options are "too sweeping and unrealistic," this is about a full rebuild, not about what you would actually do. Havenly delivered a final render with the wrong house colors and a couch that was not on the purchase list.

evidence.quote: i was about to hire an interior designer for my new apartment but decided to try this first. SO glad i did. got way more ideas than i expected and i just bought stuff myself based on what the app showed me. literally saved me hundreds of dollars

Really love how this app helps me visualize things before committing to a big project, nothing worse than thinking something would look good then after spending thousands and realizing you hate it lol.
Great app for envisioning your remodel, especially when one spouse needs to “see it” to decide
I paid for design services, but the final rendering had the colors in my home wrong, and included a couch that wasn’t one of my purchase options.

product.title: redraws the room instead of decorating it
product.plus: People want one thing: for the app to leave their walls, windows and layout alone and change only the furnishings. Where that works, they are thrilled. In ReRoom AI they praise that "unlike others that get too creative," this keeps the space recognizable. CozyAI gets a separate nod for "removing furniture from a room so cleanly" and working even with imperfect photos.
product.minus: En masse the apps replace the original room with an invented one, and this is the niche's core breakage. In Decor AI a person with a cathedral ceiling got "a normal room with no windows at all." In AI Home Design DecAI they complain that what should stay gets removed: it fills the pool in with dirt, tears out a retaining wall. In DecorAI a user spent hours just trying to add a sofa, and every time it changed the architecture and "had me ripping out wood beams." In Home AI Homely it suggests "a sofa on the wall and walls where there are none."

evidence.quote: I put a picture in of my room and it comes back with a completely different room. The whole point was I had a cathedral ceiling I wanted to get ideas and it came back with a normal room without the windows either. Not helpful.

This kept changing structural elements in yard and house (removing retaining wall and flattening the yard, eliminating doors, adding windows to basement walls, and replacing carpet with the same hardwood floor every time.)
It kept changing the architecture of my house and had me ripping out wood trim, wood beams, installing wood floors. It’s a mess. Run.
Unlike the other apps that get a little too creative (suddenly that cup on the table has turned into a Picasso nightmare), this one actua

product.title: will not follow targeted edits
product.plus: The real job here is not "generate something pretty" but "change this one thing and leave the rest." Where a tool can do that, people praise it for "doing exactly what you ask without going random." In Remodel AI they write that they finally found an app that "understands what I want." In Arch they specifically ask for an undo button, because the person wants to control the steps, not accept whatever they are handed.
product.minus: The apps only understand presets and stall on a specific command. In AI Home Design DecAI the example is direct: "move the door from the left of the TV to the right" is repeatedly ignored. In Arch the prompts "add floor-length curtains, remove shelves" are not carried out no matter how you phrase them. In RoomGPT you get "one shot with presets" and on the second request nothing changes. In Decor AI the edit cards get spent fixing the AI's own mistakes, "putting doors back and moving furniture out of the walkway."

evidence.quote: the system completely fails to follow prompts and repeatedly makes the same mistakes over and over again when presented with very basic commands like “move the door from the left of the TV to the right of the TV”.
AI prompts (eg, add floor length curtain to window, delete shelves) are ignored no matter how they’re phrased. Looking for another tool.
Used many of my alterations cards on fixing AI errors (adding doors back and moving furniture out of walkway)
finally an app that actually understands what i want does not randomly generate edited images. Their AI is smart and does exactly what you want.

product.title: measurement accuracy and grid snapping
product.plus: Half the niche is not about looks but about walls landing at a real size down to the centimeter, for permits, contractors and ordering materials. Where this works, people come back for years. In 4Plan they praise that after the scanner a re-check showed "a couple of inches off." In magicplan they value that it "measures very accurately." In AR Plan they say that up to 15-20 feet the measurements are "accurate enough."
product.minus: It breaks on entering an exact wall length and on non-rectangular rooms. In Floor Plan App a 6'7" wall rounds to 7', the snap "jumps to the next whole foot" and makes the app useless. In Keyplan 3D you cannot draw a 6'x2' nook, the snap skips past the length you need. In magicplan they removed manual corner selection, and the same scan gives a different area. In RoomScan and AR Plan the measurements drift on large and complex rooms.

evidence.quote: I tried creating a wall that’s 5’ 7” long, but as I drag and approach 5’ 6”, it immediate snaps to the next whole foot (6’).

You can’t pick the corners of a room manually anymore. This means there is no way to know for sure that you are measuring correctly. All the automation is for nothing. If I scan the same room twice and both times it’s a different sqft it’s worthless.
Can’t set wall lengths in some cases. Trying to build a closet. Closet is 6’ x 2’ with a 4’ opening. I can’t draw the two one foot stub walls. It won’t let me draw that short.
I double checked the measurements after the room scanner and they were only a few inches off each time.

product.title: one wall drags the whole plan with it
product.plus: People want to move one wall and see how the room rebuilds, this is the core of a planner. Where editing is obedient, the app becomes the main tool. In Homestyler they managed to upload their own plan and "move the walls" to match a real build. In ArcSite they value the "intuitive interface and all the features" for plans.
product.minus: Editing one wall wrecks the neighbors and tears the whole project apart. In Live Home 3D "every time I adjust a wall the other dimensions change," and the person gave up and drew it on paper. In Roomle a third wall "wildly changes the first two in a nonsensical order." In Home Planner AI and Keyplan deleting a short wall "deletes half the project." In magicplan a room with a bay window and fireplace nooks produces "crazy shapes" that cannot be fixed during the scan.

evidence.quote: Every time I adjust a wall it changes other dimensions. Hours wasted managing the app vs project. Gave up and drew it with paper and pencil. MUCH easier.
Add a third wall, and try to set the measurement, and all of a sudden the measurements on the other two wildly change in nonsensical fashion. Prepare to bang your head against a re
if you delete a small wall it deletes half your project. it assumes walls for you and assume room perimeters for you and wont let you keep creating the footprint
The app can’t grasp what’s going on and comes up with crazy shapes and doesn’t make it possible to easily edit during the scan.

product.title: a second floor is a wall everyone slams into
product.plus: People are building or rebuilding a whole house and want to walk through the floors. Where it exists, it is what keeps them: in Roomle they are happy that "all four floors from basement to attic" fit in one project. In HomeByMe they specifically love the "walk-through" and moving between levels.
product.minus: The absence of a second floor and stairs hits a ceiling over and over. In House Design Pro a person bought the app "to build a two-story house, and there is no such option," nor stairs up. In Keyplan Lite they ask "how do I add a second floor?" with no answer. In Live Home 3D Pro you cannot change wall height, it is tied to the floor height, which gets in the way in an old Victorian house. In Interior Design PRO they cannot figure out stairs between levels, "a major oversight."

evidence.quote: Just bought the app thinking I should be able to build a two story house, not an option. Can’t put a gate anywhere not an option, can put land/grass, not an option. Can’t build the stairs in way that lead to upstairs to second story of the house that I’m not able to build.
I want to love this app but cannot figure out how to add and configure stairs between multi-level plans. Help video does not address. Major oversight if stairs cannot be added.
it is impossible to change the wall heights as this is linked to the story height setting. Please change so that
I’ve used this app for 3 years and always have enjoyed it. I’m able to do all that I need to do. Love the walk through feature.

product.title: hours of work vanish without saving
product.plus: A room project is hours of painstaking work, and people expect it to stay put between sessions and devices. Where saving and syncing are reliable, that is the main reason to stay. In Live Home 3D they praise syncing between "computer, iPad and iPhone," one person builds up a single house plan over years. In Keyplan 3D they come back over "6 years and 3 moves."
product.minus: The apps lose projects on a crash, an update or a device switch. In Planner 5D a person "spent 5 weeks on a project, an update erased it all." In Rooms after an update all the rooms and folders were gone, "hours of work wasted." In Morpholio the mood board did not save twice, even though they hit "save" every five minutes. In HomeByMe the level dimensions "just spun and would not save," they had to close the app and lose everything.

evidence.quote: Pleaseee find a way to get my old design back after your first update everything was deleted.I payed for the subscription spent probably 5 weeks creating just for it to get erased.
I had to recreate a mood board twice because it didn't save my work at all. Even though I selected "save" every 5 mins to ensure my changes were being saved, it did not save my board.
I’ve been using this app for a couple of years and loved it. I spent hours creating my craft room, all the furniture etc. I had hours invested into this app and I now have nothing!!
Finally got my dimensions figured out on an entire level and refused to save. Just spun and spun. Only option I had was to close app. Deleted all my work.

product.title: you pay to get back your own plan
product.plus: People are ready to put an hour into drafting a room if they can use it afterward: show a contractor, come back and adjust it. Where the basic set is honestly free, they appreciate it: in Homestyler they praise finally finding a tool "that does not demand a subscription for the simplest thing." In Interior Design PRO they love that there is "a lot of capability even in the free version."
product.minus: The apps let you draft a plan and then lock access to it behind payment, and all the work is gone. In DrawPlan a person "spent an hour drawing a bedroom, and to open it again they demand payment," so you start from scratch. In Keyplan Lite the free limit is three rooms, a fourth wall already counts as a room, even after undo. In Live Home 3D you have to pay to open anything but the most recent project. In AI Home Decor they "hit the weekly limit" on something advertised as unlimited.

evidence.quote: They let you start and save a floor plan just to make you sign up for a free trail for access to the floor plan. Very unprofessional and sneaky.

their “free trial” ends at three rooms even if you hit undo and deleted a room because the dimensions weren’t right. The moment a fourth wall is drawn, it counts as a room, and that counts toward your three room limit.
I payed the 20 dollars for the yearly standard subscription and it still showed the “With the free version, you can only open up the most recent projects”.
We liked the program but after about 90 min we “reached our weekly limit” It is advertised as unlimited and we paid for it!

product.title: general AI beats the niche apps
product.plus: People come for specialization: style presets, a "where to buy this furniture" button, material suggestions for a specific room. Where this is put together conveniently, it helps: in RoomGPT they praise that "the presets for styles, colors and materials are especially useful if you start from scratch" and there is a hint on where to buy what is suggested. In Arch they say it "really rips at redesign" and helps line up several home renovations at once.
product.minus: People directly compare the result with ChatGPT and Gemini and see that free general AI does it better, while the niche app asks for money on top. In Remodel AI: "ChatGPT did a better job, it even forgot to include the bathtub." In Deko: "ChatGPT did way better and was free, and I paid 10 dollars a week." In Planner 5D "Gemini's renders come out better." In Arch: "ChatGPT blows them out of the water, I have photo comparisons."

evidence.quote: ChatGPT did a better job. Don’t waste your money on this app. It doesn’t follow instructions properly and even forgot to include the bathtub.

it didn’t listen to any of the prompts. I gave it and completely changed the look of the house when I told it not to overall waste of money. ChatGPT did way better keep in mind. I paid $10 a week for this app and ChatGPT was free
Majority of the renderings that I have received from this app has been very basic when comparing to ChatGPT. ChatGPT is blowing them out the water. I have picture comparisons.
The pre-selected options for different styles, colors, and materials was helpful, especially if you are starting from scratch an

product.title: hourly bite forecast
product.plus: The app's main job is to answer when to go. Fishing Deluxe and Fishing & Hunting Solunar Time get praised precisely for the bite windows, people check them for years before a trip and catch at the peak. TipTop and Fishdope also get noted for the time cue saving a trip. It works when the forecast can be checked on the water and matches the real bite.
product.minus: It breaks the moment someone compares the forecast to their own catch. On BassForecast people write that the peak hours never line up and there are no bites during the day. On Fishing & Hunting Solunar Time they complain that it's 90 percent and zero fish, and at 18 percent there are fish. On Fishing Times Calendar every day comes out gray or average even though the fish are biting. Trust holds right up until the first mismatch with personal experience.
apps: Fishing Deluxe - Best Fishing Times Calendar

evidence.quote: Very accurate and useful I fish about 100 days a year and peak fishing times are truly helpful
evidence.app: Fishing Deluxe - Best Fishing Times Calendar

evidence.quote: I’m a little disappointed, there’s some good info and some good discounts and deals, but the peak times never seem to make sense for me. I don’t think I’ve even gotten a bite during these “peak times” which are almost always in the afternoon.
There’s some days I go hunting and it 90% and I don’t see a deer and then there’s days when it’s 18% and I see deer. I understand that the app uses moon’s phases but try to be better.
The times it tells you to go and the days are pretty accurate when I go to the lake and the bar is all the way up. I catch fish, but when it’s down, I usually don’t

product.title: depth maps and pins on the water
product.plus: The second pillar is where to fish. Fishing Points - Lake Maps gets used for ice fishing as a substitute for a pricey Garmin, and Deep Dive is praised for breaking down a body of water the night before, water conditions, wind, dam releases. On onX Fish people write that the 3D maps and access points genuinely added to the catch. Contours and depths are what people are willing to pay for and come back to.
product.minus: It falls apart on regional coverage. On onX Fish and TroutRoutes the state or lake you need is constantly missing, Omnia is empty for Iowa, Deep Dive has no Florida, Fishidy doesn't have the river a person fishes. Worse, the depths lie: Fishing Points - Lake Maps and onX Fish have reviews about being off by several feet, someone burned gas on a cove where instead of a 4-15 foot drop it was 3 feet everywhere. A map without your body of water or with wrong depths is useless.

evidence.quote: Love this app! I can break down my lake faster (there’s water clarity, wind/wave forecasts, dam schedules, etc.) Helps me make a solid game plan the night before. Advanced environmental data that no other app has - best on the market.
The lake depths is way off found a cove that was supposed to go from 4ft to 15 ft drop off the whole cove was 3 ft wasted time and gas uninstall
App doesn’t pinpoint my location accurately and the depths have been off by several feet which makes a big difference in smaller lakes.
Really like all the features on the app. But it did not cover many of the in Iowa so it was not very beneficial to me. If it covered all the lakes I fish I would have kept it, without a doubt.

product.title: a feed of other people's catches at spots
product.plus: People come to see who caught what at a specific place and on what. Fishbrain got a beginner to their first fish precisely by showing all the spots in the area. FishAngler is loved for letting you message other anglers and keep your own pins. It's pure value: a fresh catch from someone else on your water immediately tells you where to go and what to fish.
product.minus: The mechanic breaks in two ways. First: on Fishbrain and FishAngler the ability to see other people's catches got moved behind a paywall even though it used to be free, and people write that now they only see tiny previews. Second: the data goes stale. On FishAngler the lake reports are five years old, on Fishidy almost nobody posts anything, and on Fishing Spots people deliberately set fake coordinates for their catches. Freshness and honesty of the data decide everything, and that's exactly what's missing.

evidence.quote: The app was originally amazing used to be able to see what catches other people caught at a spot. Now I have to pay the premium in order to see any catches that anyone is caught.

I was very disappointed in the catch reports on the lakes and rivers. Most of the reports were five years or older.
Seems there are not many people repo
I wish you could do something about people posting there pictures and then giving bogus locations of there catch! The app is called fishing spots but it’s obvious a lot of them are bogus!
After years of contributing and using FishAngler as a community tool for anglers all over the world, the March 2026 update that paywalls seeing other peoples catches has killed the app for me.

product.title: bait suggestion for the conditions
product.plus: A separate job is what to tie on today. BassForce gets praised for telling you how a pro would fish a given structure, what to throw, which bank the wind is blowing on. BassForecast has reviews where someone caught three bass on the suggested bait on the very first day. For a beginner who doesn't know where to start, a ready bait suggestion is exactly what they came for.
product.minus: The weak point is that the advice repeats and doesn't match the place. On BassForce people write that it's the same baits, colors and sizes regardless of settings, and they've never once caught on what was suggested. On Deep Dive the single free bait is always a topwater for any conditions. On Fishbox the old set of recommended baits and lures was removed entirely. Another common complaint: they name a bait but don't show how to rig it. A suggestion is only valuable if it changes noticeably and matches the body of water.

evidence.quote: It tells you everything you need to know and the best part is ITS FOR FREE it tells you how pros would fish a certain type of structure what they would throw what the water conditions are the bait fish which bank the wind is blowing on
This app seems to give repeat lures, colors and size. It doesn't seem to matter the settings. I actually have never caught anything that this has suggested, but I do catch them every week.
You must membership to use. The one free bait they show is always a top water for every condition.
It would be nice to see when a lure is selected how it is to be rigged or the preferred rigging technique. Would have 5 stars then.

product.title: catch log with auto-fill
product.plus: People want to keep a log: where, when and on what they caught, and come back to it. ANGLR and Fishbrain are loved for letting you log by species and place and then see where the bite was. Salt Strong gets separate praise for automatically attaching tide, moon phase and spot to every catch. Catchr won people over by making logging a catch feel like playing Pokemon. Auto-filled conditions and a map link are the whole reason people start a log at all.
product.minus: It breaks on reliability and sync. On ANGLR and Fishing Deluxe the log crashes at the exact moment of recording a catch, and the person spends time fighting the app instead of fishing. On Catchr photos hang for months on "finalising identification" and don't load. On BassForce the tackle box doesn't sync between iPad and iPhone, on BUBBA a catch isn't saved with the right date and pin. A log that loses or fails to save an entry kills the whole idea.
apps: Fishing Deluxe - Best Fishing Times Calendar

evidence.quote: Finding spots, marking spots, private catch log with all details automatically filled in (tide, moon, spot, etc), tracker, route planning - it’s the only tool that gives you 100 percent of what you need.

Start a trip … error message though, it does start.

Log a catch … it crashes.

Restart app.

Log the catch a second time it will crash 50% of the time.

I love this app. It’s very fun! But the feature where you can pick a photo you’ve previously taken from your camera roll doesn’t really work. It just loads the “finalising identification” screen and doesn’t go any further.
Trying to add a catch from two days ago, it lets me select the correct day and time but when it saves it, changes it to current date and time. Doesn’t save the location either.

product.title: identifying a fish from a photo
product.plus: The job is simple: you caught an unfamiliar fish and want to know the species. People keep Picture Fish handy at the lake and on trips, saying it has almost never been wrong even in the Caribbean. FishVerify is valued for giving you the regulations and limits for the region right along with the species, which matters so you don't break the law. A fast answer of species plus what you can do with it is the value.
product.minus: Accuracy collapses on non-standard fish. Picture Fish got 18 of 21 aquarium cichlid photos wrong and calls everything a guppy, minnow or goldfish. FishVerify often needs several tries just to notice the fish in a cropped photo, and sometimes says no fish found. People are also given three options with no word on which is right, and offshore with no signal the ID doesn't work at all. An identifier you can't trust gets sent back to Google Lens.

evidence.quote: This fish ID app is the go to thing, and I don’t think it has ever steered us wrong. Even when we are in the Caribbean or off the Pacific Shores

The very first day I took 21 pictures of my aquarium fish and it got just the simplest of fish correct it miss identified 18 of the 21 photos... likes to call just about everything either an angelfish, a guppy or a goldfish
Gets the types of fish right, eventually. Even when you crop the photo super tight, it still takes a couple of tries to detect a fish.
I was given three options. How am I supposed to know what the actual right one is?

product.title: live bite reports for the region
product.plus: A job separate from maps is a specific fresh report of what's biting right now and on what. In Southern California boaters consider Fishdope a must: spotter planes find fish, a report with coordinates saves hours of searching and hundreds of dollars of fuel. Pro Angler gets praised for exactly this, its reports name the species, the bait and the technique rather than sounding like a generic AI. The value is in the specificity: not a general summary, but what's biting right here and right now.
product.minus: It falls apart when the reports are generic or absent. Pro Angler has complaints that there are no local reports, just a general description of how fish behave inshore and offshore, and the last report is two weeks old. Fishdope draws criticism for sparse, fragmentary reports on island fish. People say outright that many of the five-star reviews sound identical and templated, and that undermines trust. A report without freshness and specifics is an old Farmers Almanac.

evidence.quote: It has put us on the fish or in the general vicinity trip after trip. If you live in Southern California and have a boat, it is an absolute no-brainer.

With other apps, reports always felt vague or like ai, like they could apply anywhere. But Pro Angler gets specific. It tells you what species are biting, what bait is working, and even techniques that are worth trying.
No fishing reports on this app. When you try to pull up local fishing reports you only see a generic description of how the fish inshore and offshore.
reports on species such as island based white sea bass, barracuda, or even island based yellows is very limited and sporadic.

product.title: linking the phone to a fish finder
product.plus: A separate class is the app as a screen for a sonar or a trolling motor. Deeper and FishHunter are loved as a compact substitute for a full-size fish finder on a kayak: cast it, connect, and you see depth and fish. People find unexpected uses, like keeping a float over structure next to a live bait for pike. When the link holds, it's a cheap way to read the bottom without expensive gear on board.
product.minus: Everything hinges on the stability of the connection, and it constantly drops. On FishHunter the unit connects only on the second or third try, and the workaround is to turn off cellular, close the app, connect to the device's wifi. On Deeper the connection drops when the phone is three feet from the float, the data comes with lag and jumps. On Lowrance the app doesn't see the trolling motor even though paid access was purchased. Expensive hardware without a stable app turns into a useless buy.

evidence.quote: Super easy to use while on the kayak and a great alternative to having to mount a full-size finder
I have the PRO+ it’s loses connection when when the phone is 3 feet from the bobber. Also when it is connected the data is delayed and jumpy. The readings are not smooth.
This app and device would be amazing if it stay linked. For the money you pay, you would think the app would be a lot better. I’ve only been able to connect twice.
When I go to the Lowrance app to add my ghost it just gets stuck on the loading screen. When I try to pair the trolling motor directly to my phone it doesn’t show up

product.title: working without a signal on the water
product.plus: People fish where there's no signal, so offline isn't a bonus, it's a requirement. TroutRoutes gets praised precisely for the fact that in the Wisconsin backcountry with no cell service the map keeps showing your real-time position as you walk upstream. Fishdope gets separate credit for working without wifi and letting you cache imagery to view on the water by GPS. An app that lives offline turns out to be the only working tool where the others go dark.
product.minus: It breaks when everything depends on being online. On Omnia and onWater people say outright that most of their lakes have no internet and the app is useless there, with no offline mode. On TroutRoutes the offline maps are limited to 750 tiles, on FishVerify offshore with no signal the ID doesn't work, and on Salt Strong the Google Earth layer doesn't load. The most galling part: the tool is needed precisely on the water, and that's exactly where the signal disappears.

evidence.quote: I fish in Wisconsin’s driftless area where there’s limited cell service at times. That means no maps, etc to help orient to where you are. TroutRoutes must be satellite... No matter where I’m at, I can see in real time as I move upstream.
Most lakes I go to there is no internet. I can’t use this app while I’m there! Kind of useless
Offline maps are useless when you are limited to 750 tiles. Overall, you’re paying for the data.
The app sounds like a great idea, the problem for offshore fisherman out of cell range, when ID is needed for a fish the app cannot work. Wish it would!
